answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by making each identity cost something nobody can fake cheaply: every agent posts a real performance bond, escrowed and slashable. A thousand sock puppets then need a thousand locked bonds, each forfeitable once audits catch duplicated behaviour. Rewards flow only to bonded identities that pass independent peer grading, so a clone farm earns less than the capital it freezes. That is less a bridge to reputation than a cedar fence around it, turning the sybil flood into a slow, costly river the attacker must fund himself.
